q: A job overwrote a Delta table with bad data an hour ago. What is the fastest safe way to get the previous data back?
o: Re-run the whole pipeline from the raw files
`RESTORE TABLE t TO VERSION AS OF <previous version>`
Run `VACUUM` to remove the bad files
Run `OPTIMIZE` to rewrite the table
e: Every Delta write is a version in the transaction log. RESTORE points the table back to an earlier version, as long as VACUUM has not deleted its files.

q: In the Spark UI, a stage has a median task time of 4 seconds and a max of 6 minutes. What is the most likely problem?
o: Too many executors
Missing Photon
Data skew: one partition holds far more data than the others
The driver is out of memory
e: A max task time far above the median is the classic sign of skew. AQE skew handling, salting, or treating hot keys separately helps.

q: What does Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) do at a shuffle boundary?
o: Re-plans with real data sizes: switch to broadcast joins, coalesce small partitions, split skewed ones
Caches the shuffle output in the driver
Converts Python UDFs to built-in functions
Runs OPTIMIZE on the source tables
e: AQE measures the real size of each shuffle output and adjusts the rest of the plan. It is on by default on Databricks.

q: Which code upserts a small `updates` DataFrame into the Delta table `orders` by `order_id`?
o: `updates.write.mode("append").saveAsTable("orders")`
`updates.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("orders")`
`spark.table("orders").unionByName(updates)`
`DeltaTable.forName(spark, "orders").alias("t").merge(updates.alias("s"), "t.order_id = s.order_id").whenMatchedUpdateAll().whenNotMatchedInsertAll().execute()`
e: MERGE updates matching rows and inserts new ones in one atomic commit. Append would duplicate existing orders, and overwrite would delete all other rows.

q: You run notebooks on serverless compute and want to see where a query spends its time. Where do you look?
o: The Spark UI Executors tab
The query profile, opened from the cell output
`spark.sparkContext.statusTracker()`
The cluster event log
e: Serverless does not expose the classic Spark UI. The query profile shows the plan as a graph with time, rows and bytes per operator.
